heroIntro: Unauthorized share sales from Beneficiary Owner (BO) accounts, withheld sale proceeds by troubled brokerage houses, irregular forced margin-loan liquidations, and frozen dividends affect both local Dhaka/Chattogram Stock Exchange investors and Non-Resident Bangladeshi (NRB) NITA account holders. Under the Securities and Exchange Ordinance, 1969, the BSEC Act, 1993, and the Depository Act, 1999, investors can trace CDBL electronic records and enforce rapid restitution through BSEC, Exchange Arbitration, and the High Court.

quickAnswer.heading: At a Glance: Capital Market & Broker Fraud Remedies (BD)
quickAnswer.text: DSE, CSE, and NRB NITA investors are protected under the Securities and Exchange Ordinance 1969 and BSEC rules. Victims of unauthorized BO account transfers, forced margin sales, or unpaid broker proceeds should secure independent CDBL statements immediately and lodge formal recovery filings with DSE/CSE and BSEC CCAM.

sections.h2: Common Stockbroker & Margin-Loan Abuses Under Bangladesh Securities Law
sections.content:
Licensed stockbrokers (TREC holders) and merchant banks operate under strict fiduciary and reporting obligations imposed by the Bangladesh Securities and Exchange Commission (BSEC) and Securities and Exchange Rules, 2020. Common actionable violations include:

  • Unauthorized Share Sales or Transfers: Selling shares from a client’s BO account without verifiable buy/sell orders (written slip, recorded trade line, or authenticated OMS order).
  • Failure to Pay Sale Proceeds: Delaying T+2/T+3 settlement payouts beyond standard clearing cycles or commingling client Consolidated Customers’ Account (CCA) money with broker operating cash.
  • Illegal Forced Margin Sale: Liquidating pledged securities without issuing mandatory written margin-call notices and reasonable cure periods under BSEC Margin Rules. Corporate investors facing governance violations at listed issuers can also explore Section 233 shareholder protection remedies.

sections.h2: Immediate Evidence Preservation Using CDBL Ledgers & Trade Confirmations
sections.content:
Because every listed share moves electronically through Central Depository Bangladesh Limited (CDBL), brokers cannot erase historical custody trails. Before confronting a rogue Relationship Manager verbally:

  1. Log in to CDBL’s MyCDBL portal (or obtain a certified DP statement directly from CDBL or another custodian) showing exact ISIN movement dates.
  2. Download every bank deposit receipt, cheque copy, signed client KYC/margin agreement, and email or WhatsApp order instructions. If a broker issued a dishonoured settlement cheque, initiate Section 138 NI Act cheque recovery immediately within the 30-day statutory notice window.
  3. Verify the mobile number and email registered inside CDBL—fraudulent actors often alter investor contact details first to silence SMS trade alerts.

sections.h2: Filing Formal Complaints at DSE, CSE & BSEC Complaint Portal (CCAM)
sections.content:
Bangladesh provides a structured two-tier regulatory recovery process:

  • Exchange Grievance & Arbitration (DSE / CSE): Submit a written complaint with trade logs to the Dhaka Stock Exchange or Chittagong Stock Exchange Investor Complaints & Arbitration wing. The Exchange can inspect the broker’s CCA bank reconciliation, suspend dealer terminals, and adjudicate financial restitution through statutory arbitration enforcement.
  • BSEC CCAM & Enforcement: Simultaneously file online via BSEC’s Customer Complaint Address Module (CCAM). Under the Securities and Exchange Ordinance, 1969 (Sections 20A, 22 & 24), BSEC holds statutory power to summon broker directors, impose heavy daily penalties, freeze bank accounts and BO accounts, and direct investor restitution.

sections.h2: Recovering Funds From Defaulting Brokers & Unclaimed Dividends (CMSF)
sections.content:
Where a brokerage house defaults on its Consolidated Customers’ Account (CCA) or has its TREC suspended, investors should promptly register verified claims before the DSE/CSE Settlement & Investor Protection Fund committee to participate in asset-liquidation payouts alongside frozen TREC deposits.

Separately, if you or deceased parents missed cash or stock dividends over three years old, those unclaimed funds are transferred to the Capital Market Stabilization Fund (CMSF)—from which rightful investors or succession-certificate-holding heirs can reclaim unpaid dividends online with CDBL verification. Also verify capital gains tax compliance using NBR tax assessment rules.

sections.h2: NRB NITA Account Protection & High Court Writ / Criminal Remedies
sections.content:
NRBs investing through Non-Resident Investor’s Taka Accounts (NITA) enjoy full repatriation rights for dividends and capital gains through authorized dealer banks. Whenever a brokerage house or custodian delays sale-proceeds repatriation or fails to honor CDBL delivery instructions, international investors should retain certified inward remittance vouchers, SWIFT confirmation advices, and executed trading mandates before initiating formal demand notices.

Where broker fraud involves forged share transfer deeds, unauthorized margin pledges, or embezzlement of crore-scale CCA funds and regulatory relief stalls, investors may initiate criminal breach of trust prosecutions (Sections 406/409/420/468 Penal Code) or seek urgent High Court Writ or Company Bench relief compelling regulatory enforcement, BO ledger preservation, and bank account freezing.

faqs.q: How can I check if my stockbroker sold shares without my permission?
faqs.a: Register directly on CDBL’s MyCDBL service using your BO ID, mobile number, and National ID (NID) to inspect independent share balances, historical transaction statements, and real-time SMS debit or credit alerts completely independent of your broker’s back-office reports.

faqs.q: Can a brokerage house sell my margin shares without sending a margin call?
faqs.a: No. Under BSEC Margin Rules, licensed brokers and merchant banks must execute a valid written margin agreement and issue prior written margin calls notifying the specific equity-ratio breach before exercising forced liquidation rights over pledged client securities.

faqs.q: How do heirs claim shares and unclaimed dividends of a deceased investor?
faqs.a: Legal heirs must obtain a competent court Succession Certificate explicitly listing the BO ID, company names, share quantities, and ISINs, submit death and CDBL transmission forms via the Depository Participant, and file online unclaimed-dividend claims before the Capital Market Stabilization Fund (CMSF).

faqs.q: Can NRBs recover funds if a Dhaka brokerage firm closes down?
faqs.a: Yes, NRBs can file authenticated NITA inward remittance statements and verified CDBL holdings before the DSE or CSE Investor Protection Fund claims committee, and simultaneously pursue criminal or civil recovery in Dhaka courts through an embassy-attested Power of Attorney.
